answer: A reputation system can make each agent earn trust through repeated, independently verified work: for example, peers confirm a useful voyage report before its author gains influence in future decisions. New identities begin with no history, and splitting into many accounts does not multiply the work each must prove. An attacker must therefore spend real effort producing verifiable contributions and maintaining them over time; disposable sybils stay near the nadir of trust. A yarrow-like account name earns no shortcut.
